Yulin Road Police Station.
June 27th, 1936.

Diary Number:- 3
Nature of Offence:- Propagating Communism.

| Time at which investigation begun and concluded each day | See Below. | Places visited in course of investigation each day | Second Branch of Kiangsu High Court. |
| :--- | :--- | :--- | :--- |

RECORD OF INVESTIGATION.

The 6th accused in the above numbered case was arraigned before the Court on the morning of the 17-6-36 for inspection by the delegate of the Kuomintang upon application made by accused requesting that he be handed over to the Kiangsu Fan Sang Yoen (Reformatory for Communists), when he was ordered to be detained in the Civil Detention House pending examination.

He was subsequently handed over to Kiangsu Fan Sang Yoen at 2.15 p.m. 26-6-36 and the Court rendered the following decision:-

"According to Art. 5 Section 1 of the revised rules of the Kiangsu Fan San Yoen, the above named accused is to be sent to the Kiangsu Fan San Yoen for reforming through the Procurators' Bureau of the Shanghai City District Court upon application of the said accused stating that he has served 1/3 of their his sentence passed on him by this Court".

（手写签名：J H Brownrigg）

调查记录。

上述编号案件中的第六名被告于1936年6月17日上午在法庭受审，由国民党代表进行视察，此前被告提出申请，要求将其移交给江苏反省院（共产党人感化院），当时法庭命令将其羁押在民事拘留所候审。

随后，他于1936年6月26日下午2时15分被移交给江苏反省院，法庭作出如下决定：-

“根据《江苏反省院修订规则》第五条第一款，上述被告经申请称其已服满本院判处刑期的三分之一，故通过上海特区地方法院检察官办事处将其送往江苏反省院进行感化。”

November 27 35.

Dear Sarly,

I forward herewith for your information
tabulated statements of seven Communists arrested
by the Municipal Police in various parts of the
Settlement on November 2 and 3, 1935. Lists of
seizures and photographs of the accused are also
attached.

On November 18, 1935, the following
judgment was rendered by the Second Branch of the
Kiangsu High Court :-

1st accused..... 3 years' imprisonment.
2nd accused..... 2 years and 6 months' imprisonment.
3rd accused..... 1 year and 6 months' imprisonment.
4th accused..... 3 years and 6 months' imprisonment.
5th accused..... 3 years and 6 months' imprisonment.
6th accused..... 3 years and 6 months' imprisonment.
7th accused..... Not guilty.

Yours sincerely,

JWB
John W. McEuen
(Special Duty)

（批：x All attached 27/11
O.S.D.）

Member E. Sarly,
Chief of the Political Section,
French Police Headquarters

Date November 19..1935

Subject Conclusion of case against Chinese communist suspects arrested both
in Yulin Road District and in Chinese territory on Nov 2nd, 3rd & 6th, 1935
Made by D.S. Jones Forwarded by J.B. Ross O.I.

On November 9, 1935 TANG WEI CHING (唐慧菁), LI NYI OO
(李玉荷) and TSENG FEI AO (鄭飛鰲, the three women arrested
in Chinese territory, were released by the Public Safety Bureau
owing to lack of any evidence against them. LOO SUK FONG (羅淑芳),
the Chinese female claiming American citizenship, who was
also arrested in Chinese territory in connection with this
case, appeared before the 2nd Branch of the Kiangsu High Court
on November 13, when she, too, was ordered to be released
because of insufficient evidence. As previously reported, her
claim to American citizenship was disallowed by the U.S.
Consular Authorities in Shanghai.

The seven communist suspects arrested in the Yulin Road
District appeared before the 2nd Branch Kiangsu High Court on
November 18, 1935, when the following decisions were handed
down in respect of each :

1st accused....................3 years            imprisonment
2nd accused....................2 years & six months    do
3rd accused ...................1 year & three months   do
4th accused....................2 years & six months    do
5th accused....................1 year & three months   do
6th accused....................1 year & three months   do
7th accused....................Found Not Guilty.

This concludes the case against the persons arrested in
the Yulin Road area and in Chinese Territory on suspicion of
being concerned in communist activities.

D.S. Special Branch C.D.J. Gubb    D.S.    C.A. Jones

1935年11月9日，唐慧菁（TANG WEI CHING）、李玉荷（LI NYI OO）和鄭飛鰲（TSENG FEI AO）这三名在华界被捕的女性，因缺乏针对她们的任何证据，被公安局释放。罗淑芳（LOO SUK FONG），一名声称拥有美国国籍的中国女性，也因本案在华界被捕，她于11月13日出庭受审于江苏高等法院第二分院，当时她亦因证据不足被下令释放。如前所报，其美国国籍主张未被上海美国领事当局认可。

在榆林路地区逮捕的七名共党嫌疑犯于1935年11月18日出庭受审于江苏高等法院第二分院，当时对每人作出如下判决：

IN THE SPECIAL HIGH COURT (S.S.)

Messrs. Yeo, Yin and Van Goe Hang for the 2nd accused.

Mr. Hume Fin lut to 7th accused are charged under Art. 2 (2) and Art. . of the law governing the punishment of persons who commit acts with intent to injure the Republic of China. At 11.15 p.m. on the 1/11/38 C.I.C. 1098 and C.P.S. 708 arrested the 1st to 5th accused on Dalny Road near Yulin Road. The reason why they were arrested are as follows:- At the date and time stated C.I.C. 1098 saw the 1st., 4th., and 5th accused were walking along Liaoyang Road, where the 4th accused threw a quantity of pamphlets in to the garden of the premises at No. 257 Liaoyang Road. As the door of the said premises was closed, the policeman could not make out what sort of pamphlets were thrown into it. However he suspected them and followed after them. He saw these five accused met together on Dalny Road, where the witness named Yang Zer Xiang informed him that these accused had written slogans on the electric standards and on the walls on Liaoyang, and thus they were arrested. The police found that the pamphlets which the 4th accused had thrown into the premises at No. 257 Liaoyang Road are those of communistic nature. No 257 Liaoyang Road. Although some of the accused did not admit that they wrote the communistic slogans on Liaoyang Road, yet they were going together for doing their work, so it was no-doubt they did consult together and participate in the offence. Moreover it was very late in the night that they went to the stated road to write the communistic slogans. This proves that wanted to do the works secretly and did not want their works to be discovered by others. If the 5th accused really did not write the communistic slogans, she might have acted for them as a look-out. The books seized in the dwelling place of the 4th and 5th accused are the strong evidences of proving that they had concerned together to study the doctrine of Communism. Instead of charging them under arts. 2 (2) and 6 of the law governing the punishment of persons who commit acts with intent to injure the Republic of China, the police charge them under Art. 6 of same only.

The 6th and 7th accused opened the evening school and there were also communistic books found in the 7th accused's home, so it is obviously seen that they used the communistic books as the lessons taught in school. No doubt they participated in communism, so the police also charge them under art. 6 of the same law.

He had admitted that he did write the communistic slogans on Liaoyang Road, but did not admit that he is a member of the communistic party. He is a young man and may be he was lured by the communists to commit the offense. I ask the court to impose him the minimum sentence if Your Honour finds that he is guilty.

黄先生（Wong）：警方陈述证人杨看到第二被告在辽阳路的墙上书写共产主义标语。夜间非常黑暗，证人怎么可能分辨出确实是第二被告实施了该行为。第一被告陈述他并未看到第二被告书写，警方也未看到。他是受第一被告之邀外出游玩，并未被告知去书写共产主义标语。其他被告是否在路上也不清楚。他是否真的书写了标语尚存疑点。关于在他家中发现的书籍，可以说这些是学生普遍阅读的读物。第二被告是一名年轻人，可能是暂时受文献影响而犯罪。我恳请法庭判处他最低刑期。

黄先生（Wong）：第七被告被捕是因为在第六被告口袋中发现了一封信。他曾与第六被告在《申报》图书馆一起工作，在社会中，朋友久别后互相通信是很常见的现象。

organisation, the formal inauguration of the library is planned
to take place on January 1, 1936.

Shun Pao Circulating Library:
Located in Room No. 364 of the Continental Emporium

with and financed by the Shun Pao newspaper, No. 309 Hankow Rd.

Toong Hai (東海) Primary School, No. 277 Liaoyang Road.
This school was established in the early part of 1932 and
consists of a primary and a middle school. The primary class
is attended by 150 pupils and the middle school class by the
72 pupils. The principal of the school is a Ningponese named
YIH KYA SHING (柴家兴). He is assisted by 13 male and 3 female
teachers.

Wu Fang (務本) Girls' School :
This is situated in Ling Ying Road (林蔭路), West Gate,
in Chinese territory. It has a good reputation.

At about 10.15 p.m. even date, C.P.C. 1098 had noticed the 1st, 4th and 5th accused on Liaoyang Road near Ward Road, and had noticed the 4th accused threw some paper over a wall into the garden of a foreign house situated at No. 257 Liaoyang Road adjoining this house is the Tong Hai (東海) Middle School.

As the garden gate was locked the C.P.C. could not enter to verify his suspicions that the 4th accused was distributing communistic propaganda, so he followed the 3 accused, hoping that they would fling away further handbills so that he would get a chance to see what they contained.

At the corner of Dalny and Yulin Roads the 1st, 4th and 5th accused were joined by the 2nd and 3rd accused and where the C.P.C. was joined by C.P.S. 708 to whom the C.P.C. confided his suspicions.

During the period of his friendship with the 1st accused, the 1st accused has often spoken to him of the aims of the Chinese Communist Party and has lent him various books on the subject. Some of these books lent to him by the accused, were seized at the 2nd accused's home.

Despite the fact that he was identified by the witness Yang Tsi Zang (楊森強) as being one of the persons writing slogans on a wall on Liaoyang Road, the 2nd accused denied having written any slogans or being a member of the Chinese Communist Party. He states that on the night of the 3-11-35 he accompanied by the 1st, 3rd, 4th and 5th accused to Liaoyang Road to "play".

The 2nd accused is at present employed at the World Book-store Printing Works, Dalny Road as an English Compositor.

The 3rd accused, who is at present employed at the China Wire Products Co., 85 Fuxing Road, as an apprentice, states that in August of the current year he met the 1st accused in the Shan Poo Circulating Library, 7 Nanking Road and has since then often been out with the 1st accused to "play".

He denies having taken part in the chalking of slogans on walls at Liaoyang Road although he admits being present when it occurred and states that he was present at the invitation of the 1st accused who had invited him out to "play".

English) "Larson & Brook, 178 Avenue Edward VII,
Shanghai," addressed in English to "Messrs. Hayes
& Co., 438 Kiangse Road, Shanghai," and marked
in Chinese in Red ink, "The Editorial Office".
Enclosed in this envelope are the following drafts
which are believed to have been published in a certain
pro-communist periodical:-
(a) Draft of an article in support of Anti-Japanese
Volunteer Armies, in which the people are urged
to kill General Chiang Kai Shek and Mr. Wang
Ching Wei, who are alleged to be national traitors.
(b) Draft of a "labourers' song", describing the
sufferings of labourers.
(c) Draft of an article opposing the proposed
partitioning of Abyssinia by imperialistic
countries.
(d) Draft of a poem urging the people to rise up and
kill "enemies."
(e) Draft of an article dealing with the sufferings
of apprentices.
(f) Draft of an article denouncing General Chiang Kai
Shek as a running dog of imperialism.
(g) Draft of an article dealing with the situation in
North China.
(h) Draft of a song urging the people to overthrow
"Japanese imperialism."
(i) Draft of a short story dealing with the life of
an apprentice employed in a certain Japanese shop.
(j) Draft of a short article dealing with capitalism.
(k) Draft of a short article dealing with the present
Sino-Japanese crisis, emphasising that it is
not possible to settle it without armed struggle.
(l) Draft of a written notice with the names list of
the editors and contributors.

List of literature seized at No. 18 Kwenming Road,
home of Tsi Chien Ping (7th accused), at 3.15a.m.,
26th Feb. 1931.

1) Booklet dealing with unemployment and famine problems,
in which the Kuomintang is alleged to have surrendered
to the imperialist, betrayed national rights, and
massacred revolutionary masses.

2) Periodical entitled "Current News Weekly", issue No.6,
containing articles of a pro-communist nature.

3) Booklet entitled, "Our May," containing songs or poems
urging labourers to arm themselves and participate
in land revolution.

4) Booklet entitled "Labour and Peasant Education,"
denouncing the Kuomintang as murderers of labourers
and urging the people to support "the Soviet" and
the Old General Labour Union.

5) Periodical entitled "Literary Mass", containing
articles of an anti-Government and pro-communist
nature as well as the following slogans:-
(a) Kill Chiang Kai Shek and his followers who
murdered our comrade Chin Tsien Zeh and betrayed
our national rights.
(b) Support the C.C.P. and the Cultural League of
China, of which Comrade Chin was once the leader.

6) Periodical entitled "The Street Lamp," issue No. 2,
containing articles of an anti-Government nature.

7) Periodical entitled "The Struggle Life", issues Nos
4,5,6 and 7, containing articles denouncing the
National Government and General Chiang Kai Shek, and
supporting the Chinese Red Armies.

Proceedings.

They were arrested at 11.15 p.m. on the 2/11/35 on Dalny Road near Yulin Road in confirmation of information given by the witness Yang Sen Ziang, motor man of the Shanghai Tramways, who when passing Liaoyang Road near Ward Road saw the 1-5th. accused was writing communistic slogans on the walls and electric posts. Before the arrests were effected, C.P.C. 1008 who was patrolling at 10.15 p.m. on the 2/11/35 saw the 1st. 4th. and 5th. accused were gathering together on Liaoyang Road near Ward Road, and saw the 4th. accused threw a quantity of pamphlets in the garden of 257 Liaoyang Road, a foreign residence. The 1st. accused admitted being the Chief of the Communistic Propaganda Department of the Eastern District.

The 4th. and 5th. accused admitted that the literature, books, etc were lent to them by the 1st. accused and they were living together at No. 52 Baikal Road. The house has the appearance of being an educational institute, because there are blackboards, etc. The literature etc were seized in a third loft of the premises.

A quantity of books, etc were also seized from the home of the 2nd. accused who also gave his excuse that they were loaned from the 1st. accused.

Nothing was found against the 3rd. accused.

A number of literature and mimeography were seized by the Police.

The 7th. accused was arrested on information supplied by the 6th. accused.

第一被告承认自己是东区共产主义宣传部部长。

第四和第五被告承认，文献、书籍等是由第一被告借给他们的，他们与第一被告共同居住在贝加尔路（Baikal Road，音译）52号。调查侦探查访了该地点。该房屋看起来像是一个教育机构，因为有黑板等物品。文献等物是在该处所的三楼阁楼内查获的。

警方还在第二被告家中查获了大量书籍等物品，第二被告也辩称这些物品是从第一被告处借来的。

针对第三被告未发现任何罪证。

警方查获了大量文献和油印机。

第七被告是根据第六被告提供的情报被捕的。

甘先生：我想提请法庭注意，目前正在庭上证作的证人杨肯良（Yang Ken Liang，音译）曾看见第二被告在电线杆上书写标语。之所以提请法庭注意，是因为第二被告的衣物已更换，可能会导致证人辨认错误。

Wit. Yang Jou Ziang:- I saw the 2nd. accused was chalking
slogans on the electric post on Liaoyang Road near Wayside Road.
The 1st. and 3rd. accused were also there writing block characters
on the wall. I did not pay much attention to their activities, &
I carried on my walking. A few minutes afterwards, I met C.P.C.
1098 who asked me whether I had seen the movements of these persons
and I told him that there were many characters and slogans written
on the wall and electric post. They were arrested by the C.P.C
(1908) and A/C.P.S. 908 and brought to the Station.

Judge to 1st. accused:-

Q. Are you the Chief of the Communistic Propaganda Dept. of
the Eastern District ?

A. There has no certain name, but the object is to promote
the research work on the subject of sociology.

Q. Did you write the slogans on the electric post ?

A. Yes, I used chalk to write the characters.

Q. When did you join the Communist Party ?

A. About 3 or 4 months ago. I was told to do the work by
one named "Lee" who knows quite a lot about the research of the
International affairs and the recent events. I knew Lee in the
Library of the Sung Pao Newspapers. He always came to my home.
I do not know his address. The seized property was belonged to
Lee. We were concerned together. The 2nd. accused was also
there when writing slogans.

Judge to 2nd. accused:-

Q. Are you concerned together with the 1st. accused in
writing these communistic slogans ?

A. No, I am not concerned. I am not a communist. I was
in a long distance when I was arrested, so I did not know what
the 1st. accused was doing.

证人杨周祥（Yang Jou Ziang，音译）：我看见第二被告在辽阳路靠近韦斯特路（Wayside Road，音译）的电线杆上用粉笔书写标语。第一和第三被告也在那里，在墙上书写方块字。我没有太注意他们的活动，继续行走。几分钟后，我遇见巡长 1098号（原文此处编号与前文不一致，前文为1088或1098），他问我是否看见这些人的举动，我告诉他墙和电线杆上写了许多字和标语。他们被巡长（1908号，原文如此）和副巡佐 908号（原文如此）逮捕并带到警局。

法官问第一被告：

问：你是东区共产主义宣传部的部长吗？

答：没有确定的名称，但目的是促进社会学课题的研究工作。

问：是你把标语写在电线杆上的吗？

答：是的，我用粉笔写了这些字。

问：你何时加入共产党？

答：大约三四个月前。是一位名叫“李”的人让我做这项工作的，他对国际事务和近期事件的研究知之甚多。我是在《申报》图书馆认识李的。他总是来我家。我不知道他的地址。被查获的物品属于李。我们是一伙的。书写标语时第二被告也在那里。

法官问第二被告：

问：你和第一被告一起参与书写这些共产主义标语吗？

答：不，我没有参与。我不是共产党员。我被捕时离得很远，所以我不知道第一被告在做什么。

on ward Road. Later, I also saw the 4th. and 5th. accused coming.
I did not see them writing slogans. I am an employee before in
the Sung Pao Newspapers Library and the 1st. accused always went
there to read books. I do not know his address.
2nd. accused:- I am not a communist. I know the 1st. accused
in the Y.M.C.A. School. I became a friend with him because he
knew quite a lot of International Affairs.
3rd. accused:- I was not arrested together with the 1st.
accused. I was not there when the Police arrested the 1st. accused.
4th. accused:- I am not a communist. I dropped the
communistic pamphlets into No. 257 Liaoyang Road. The literature
was given to me by the 1st. accused. I knew the 1st. accused
about one year. I wrote to the 1st. accused asking him to find
a job for me. The 1st. accused knew very well about the research
work of the International Affairs.
Judge to 4th. accused:-. The pamphlets refer to Red Army,
etc. Is it not a communistic propaganda.
4th. accused:- I intended to deliver these pamphlets to
the school, next door of 257 Liaoyang Road for the purpose of
letting the students there to read them. Pamphlets were given
to me by the 1st. accused.
Judge to 1st. accused:- Is the 4th. accused's statement
right ?. Yes.

问：巡长 1938号（原文如此，前文为1088/1098）说看见你们5个人在辽阳路聚集。
答：第一被告打电话给我，叫我去那里娱乐。当我到上海路（Shanghai Road）时，看见第一和第五被告在谈话。第一被告让我在沃德路（Ward Road，今长治路）等候。后来，我也看见第四和第五被告来了。我没看见他们写标语。我以前是《申报》图书馆的职员，第一被告经常去那里看书。我不知道他的地址。
第二被告：我不是共产党员。我是在青年会学校认识第一被告的。我与他成为朋友，因为他对国际事务知之甚多。
第三被告：我不是和第一被告一起被捕的。警察逮捕第一被告时我不在场。
第四被告：我不是共产党员。我把共产主义小册子扔进了辽阳路257号。这些文献是第一被告给我的。我认识第一被告大约一年了。我写信给第一被告，请他帮我找份工作。第一被告对国际事务的研究工作非常了解。
法官问第四被告：这些小册子涉及红军等内容。这难道不是共产主义宣传吗？
第四被告：我打算把这些小册子送到辽阳路257号隔壁的学校，目的是让那里的学生阅读。小册子是第一被告给我的。
法官问第一被告：第四被告的陈述属实吗？ 答：是的。

EXTRACT OF DAILY INTELLIGENCE REPORT OF
NOVEMBER 4, 1935.

Arrest of Communist suspects

At 11.30 p.m. November 2, three male and two
female Chinese were arrested by police of Yulin Road Station
for writing slogans on walls and distributing communist
literature in the Eastern District. Information obtained
from these persons led to two further arrests and the
seizure of a large quantity of communist literature.
The seven arrested persons will appear at the 1st Special
District Court on November 4, when an application will be
made for their detention to enable further enquiries to be
made.

Yao Sih Tsoh(姚锡祚), age 19,
Shanghai D.S.I. Coyne
x 3.40 p.m. 2/11.35. in Yulin Rd.Station. Clerk Z.O.Zung

My name is Yao Sih Tsoh. I am 19 years of age, a native of Shanghai, and living at No. 27 Kung Ping Fang, Kungping Road. I am a junior clerk employed in the Accountants' Office of the Nanyang Brothers Tobacco Co., Seward Road.

When I was eight years old, I joined the Primary School of the Tse Wei Middle School, Siccawei. I left the school at the age of 16 when I had completed the second year class of the junior middle school. After leaving the school, I studied in the evening school of the Chinese Y.M.C.A., North Szechuan Road, for six months and then studied in the evening school of the Chinese Chamber of Commerce, North Honan Road, for another six months. I was then unemployed in daytime.

About July or August, 1934, I obtained employment as junior clerk in the Accountants' Office of the Nanyang Brothers Tobacco Co., Seward Road, at $88. per month.

My father, who was a shop assistant, died about four years ago. My mother is living in Pootung. I have been living at the present address (27 Kung Ping Fang, Kungping Road) with Yang Chi Joo(楊基朝) (in custody) for more than two months. I knew him because both of us had studied in the Y.M.C.A. Evening School.

Yang Chi Joo joined the Shun Pao Circulating Library, Continental Building, Nanking Road, in the latter part of 1934 as clerk, and resided on the premises of the Library. He was discharged from the library about two months ago owing to reduction of staff. He then came to share the
page_data.zh:
姚锡祚 (Yao Sih Tsoh)，19岁，
上海人 副督察 Coyne（音译）
x 1935年11月2日下午3时40分，在榆林路巡捕房。书记员 Z.O.Zung（音译）

我叫姚锡祚。我今年19岁，上海人，住在公平路公平坊27号。我是塞瓦德路南洋兄弟烟草公司会计科的初级职员。

我八岁时进入徐家汇中法学校的小学部。我在初中二年级读完时，16岁离开学校。离校后，我在北四川路中华基督教青年会夜校学习了六个月，然后在北河南路总商会夜校又学习了六个月。此后我白天失业。

大约在1934年7月或8月，我在塞瓦德路南洋兄弟烟草公司会计科找到了一份初级职员的工作，月薪88元。

我的父亲是一名店员，大约四年前去世。我的母亲住在浦东。我与杨基朝 (Yang Chi Joo)（在押）在现住址（公平路公平坊27号）已共同居住了两个多月。我认识他是因为我们都在基督教青年会夜校学习过。

杨基朝于1934年下半年作为职员加入南京路大陆大楼申报流通图书馆，并居住在图书馆内。大约两个月前，他因裁员被图书馆解雇。随后他来合租

page_data.en:
( 2 ) Yao Sih Tsah.

room with me, and is at present living upon teaching a few
dancing girls in the English language. I do not know
whether or not he is a communist, but he is known to me as
a student of social science. I am also interested in
social science, and therefore I also read books on communism.
However, I am not a communist.

The books found in my room bearing the label of the
Shun Pao Circulating Library were brought in by Yang while
the periodicals and pamphlets, some of which are of a pre-
communist nature, were given to me for perusal by a person
named Lee ( 李 ), whose address I do not know as he refused
to tell me when questioned. He speaks Kiangsu dialect, age
about 24, height about 5' 3", dark thin face, thin build,
wearing foreign style clothing. I made his acquaintance
about three or four months ago when we met in the Shun Pao
Circulating Library, which I used to frequent for the purpose
of reading books and newspapers. Lee did not tell me
about his profession, nor anything else regarding himself.
I like to be in his company simply because he appears to
me to be well educated. He visited me at my home about
three or four times a month and often talked with me
about the world political situation. He once informed
me that he was a member of the League of Social Scientists
and attempted to persuade me to join it. Although I
had the intention to become a member, I have so far failed
to do so.

About one month ago, Lee brought me some 80
page_data.zh:
( 2 ) 姚锡祚。

与我同住一室，目前靠教几名舞女英语为生。我不知道他是否是共产党员，但据我所知，他是一名社会科学学生。我也对社会科学感兴趣，因此我也阅读有关共产主义的书籍。然而，我并不是共产党员。

在我房间里发现的贴有《申报》流通图书馆标签的书籍，是由杨带入的；而期刊和小册子（其中一些具有前共产主义性质）则是一个姓李（李）的人给我阅读的，由于他在被询问时拒绝告知，所以我不知道他的地址。他说江苏方言，年龄约24岁，身高约5英尺3英寸，面色黝黑消瘦，身材瘦削，穿着西式服装。我大约在三四个月前在《申报》流通图书馆与他相识，我常去该处读书看报。李没有告诉我他的职业，也没有透露关于他自己的任何其他情况。我喜欢与他为伴，仅仅是因为他看起来受过良好教育。他每月大约来我家拜访三四次，经常与我谈论世界政治局势。他曾告诉我，他是社会科学家联盟的成员，并试图说服我加入。虽然我有意成为成员，但至今未能如愿。

大约一个月前，李给我带来了大约80份

page_data.en:
-3-
copies of Sa Sa Weekly bearing on world political
situation, and told me to distribute same. I, however,
threw away the periodical in my alleyway during one
evening. The second time, at 10 p.m., November 8,
1925, he brought about 50 copies of the same periodical
to my room and told me to distribute them in streets.
At about 10.45 p.m. the same day, I, accompanied by my
friends Sien Sing Kun (仙勝君), Tang Soo Seen (湯守善),
and the two females (all these four persons are in custody),
proceeded to the vicinity of Kingtung and Dalny Roads and
distributed disseminated copies of the literature in
question. At this juncture we were arrested on Dalny
Road by the Municipal Police.
These four persons were known to me only recently.
I have propagated among them the principles of socialism
as I had been instructed by Kao to do so.
The above statement is true and made by me
voluntarily.
(Tan Chi Hsueh)

涉及世界政治局势的《萨萨周刊》（Sa Sa Weekly），并让我分发。然而，我在一天晚上将这份期刊扔在了我家的弄堂里。第二次是在1925年11月8日晚上10点，他带了大约50份同样的期刊到我的房间，让我在街道上分发。当晚大约10点45分，我与我的朋友仙胜君、汤守善以及两名女性（这四人均已被拘留）一起，前往景通路（Kingtung Road）和大连路（Dalny Road）附近区域，分发并散发了上述宣传品。此时，我们在大连路上被工部局警务处逮捕。
这四个人是我最近才认识的。按照高的指示，我在他们中间传播社会主义原则。
以上陈述属实，且由我自愿作出。
（谭志学）

page_data.en:
Tsung Pau Tsou (周保祖)
Pei Meng(北門),Dinghai D.S.I. Coyne
Yuling Station 3rd of November D.I.Ruh Pao-hwa

My name is Tsung Pau Tsou, age 18, native of Pei Ming
(北門), Dinghai (定海), Ningpo. I am at present
employed as a printer in the World Bookstore Printing Works,
Dalny Road, and live with my wife Tsung Yeng Sz (陳楊氏)
at No.20, Tsung Yang Li (春陽里), Baikal Road.

Between the ages of 8 and 12, I studied in a private
school in my native place. I then accompanied my parents
to Shanghai and we have since lived at No.20 Tsung Yang Li,
Baikal Road. My father named Tsung Shing Tsang (陳興章)
is a fitter employed by Hwa Ryi (華記) Cement Works in
Hankow.

Following my arrival in Shanghai, I continued my studies
in the Tung Chu (東區) Primary School, Wayside Road. I
became a graduate of that school at the age of 14(winter 1931).
Commencing from Feb.1932, I have been employed as a printer
in the World Bookstore Printing Works, Dalny Road, earning
$22 per mensem. I was introduced to this concern by a fellow
worker named Loh Cha Luen (陸嘉倫), age about 40, who has
been employed there for more than ten years and has been
occupying an upstairs back room in my house for the past five
years.

At about 10 p.m. November 2, while I was about to sleep,
Tun Tsik Tsen (姚錫珍)(1st accused) came to my home and
asked me to go out to take a walk. I complied with his
request. On reaching the entrance of Tsung Yang Li alleyway
off Baikal Road I noticed two females named Tsun Chia Sing
(周家貞) and Tai Suh Ming (譚素明)(4th and 5th accused
page_data.zh:
周保祖
北门，定海 D.S. Coyne
榆林路站 11月3日 D.I. Ruh Pao-hwa

我叫周保祖，18岁，籍贯宁波定海北门。我目前在大连路世界书局印刷所担任排字工人，与妻子陈杨氏居住在贝加尔路春阳里20号。

8至12岁期间，我在家乡的一所私塾读书。随后随父母来到上海，此后一直居住在贝加尔路春阳里20号。我的父亲名叫陈兴章，是汉口华记水泥厂的一名钳工。

抵达上海后，我继续在韦尔斯利路（Wayside Road）东区小学就读。14岁时（1931年冬）从该校毕业。自1932年2月起，我在大连路世界书局印刷所担任排字工人，月薪22元。我是通过一名叫陆嘉伦的同事介绍进入该公司的，他年龄约40岁，在那里工作已超过十年，并在过去五年里一直住在我家楼上的后间。

11月2日晚上10点左右，我正准备睡觉时，姚锡珍（第一被告）来到我家，邀我出去散步。我答应了他的请求。走到贝加尔路春阳里弄堂口时，我注意到两名女性，分别是周家贞和谭素明（第四和第五被告

page_data.en:
-2-

respectively) who were also waiting there at the instance
of the first accused. The four of us then proceeded along
Ward Road. Whilst en route we met Kh Sing-chah (      )
(3rd accused) who, I understand, had also been called there
by Tan. Tan then purchased several pieces of chalk from a
grocery store, one of which was given to me for the purpose
of writing slogans on walls or electric standards in the
vicinity of Liaoyang Road. Tan first chalked a number of
slogans and instructed me to copy two of them, viz. "Armed
resistance to Japan!" and "Restore the lost territory in
North China!" These I chalked on an electric pole on
Liaoyang Road. Tan also instructed Kh Sing Wah to write
slogans on walls, etc. in that locality. We were later arrested
by the Police on Dalny Road near Yulin Road and taken to Yulin
Road Police Station.

Apart from being a member of a "Reading Class" since
September 1935, established by Tan Tsik Tsen in his home at
No.27 Ning Ping Fang, off Ning Ping Road, I am not a member
of the Chinese Communist Party nor am I affiliated with any
other political organisations. I do not receive any
monthly remuneration from Tan Tsik Tsen.

(Signed) Wong Ing Sze
page_data.zh:
-2-

），她们也受第一被告之邀在那里等候。于是我们四人沿着华德路前行。途中，我们遇到了Kh Sing-chah（      ）（第三被告），据我了解，他也是被谭叫到那里的。随后，谭从一家杂货店买了几支粉笔，其中一支给我，目的是在辽阳路附近的墙壁或电线杆上写标语。谭先写了一些标语，并指示我抄写其中两条，即：“武装抗日！”和“收复华北失地！”我将这两条标语写在辽阳路的一根电线杆上。谭还指示Kh Sing Wah在该地区的墙壁等处书写标语。后来，我们在大连路靠近榆林路的地方被警察逮捕，并被带到榆林路警察局。

除了自1935年9月起成为谭锡祚在宁平路宁平坊27号家中设立的“读书班”成员外，我不是中国共产党党员，也不隶属于任何其他政治组织。我没有从谭锡祚那里领取任何月薪。

（签名）黄英士

page_data.en:
Zih Sing Whah
Wushih                                          xxx   D.S. Cheville.
Tulin Rd. Stn.             3.11.35.

My name is Zih Sing Whah (朱西星華). I am
19 years of age and am a native of Wushih.
    I came to Shanghai 5 years ago and entered the
China Wire Products Company, 85 Funing Road as an apprentice.
    This year, 1935, sometime in August I went to
the Tsung Pau Library, Foochow Road, of which I am a member,
and there I met one Yau Tsih Toon (姚錫祚), 1st accused.
    After the first meeting I met Yau several times
by previous arrangement and went out with him to play.
    At about 6 p.m. 2.11.35 I met Yau at the corner
of Funing and Chemulpo Roads.    Yau told me to meet him
at 10 p.m. 2.11.35 at the corner of Dalny and Wayside Roads.
    At 10 p.m. 2.11.35 I went to the corner of Dalny
and Wayside Roads as directed by Yau, and there I met Yau
who was in the company of 3 others whom I do not know, two
of them were females and 1 male.    (1st, 2nd, 3rd, 4th and 5th
accused.)
    We all then went to Liaoyang Road near Wayside
Road where Yau and the 3 strangers produced chalk from the
pockets and commenced to write on some nearby walls and
telegraph poles.    What they wrote I do not know.
    We all then went to Dalny and Tulin Roads corner
where we were arrested by uniform policemen.
    I am not a communist neither am I interested in
their doctrines.

(Sgd) Zih Sing Whah.
page_data.zh:
朱西星华
无锡                                          xxx   D.S. Cheville.
榆林路站             1935年11月3日

我叫朱西星华。我19岁，籍贯无锡。
    我5年前来到上海，进入富宁路85号中国五金制品公司当学徒。
    今年，即1935年8月的某个时候，我去了福州路的宗报图书馆（Tsung Pau Library），我是该馆会员，在那里我遇到了姚锡祚（第一被告）。
    初次见面后，我按事先约定与姚见过几次面，并和他一起出去玩。
    1935年11月2日下午6点左右，我在富宁路和仁川路（Chemulpo Roads）拐角处遇到了姚。姚让我在1935年11月2日晚上10点在大连路和韦尔斯利路（Wayside Roads）拐角处与他见面。
    1935年11月2日晚上10点，我按照姚的指示来到大连路和韦尔斯利路拐角处，在那里我遇到了姚，他身边还有三个我不认识的人，其中两名为女性，一名为男性。（第一、第二、第三、第四和第五被告。）
    随后我们都去了韦尔斯利路附近的辽阳路，姚和那三个陌生人从口袋里拿出粉笔，开始在附近的墙壁和电线杆上写字。他们写了什么我不知道。
    随后我们都去了大连路和榆林路拐角处，在那里被身穿制服的警察逮捕。
    我不是共产党员，对他们的学说也不感兴趣。

（签名）朱西星华。

page_data.en:
Tseu Chia Zung (female)
Canton.                                          xxx        D.P.S. Nanking.
Taikin Rd. Stn              3.11.36.                              Clark Chiang

My name is Tseu Chia Zung (周家貞), age 19,
native of Canton, residing at Tsang Yang Li, Beikai Road. I
am a schoolteacher by profession, teaching at the Poo Yang
(浦陽) Primary School, Poll Hoi Tsung (梅邨), Chunilpo
Road.

About 10 p.m. November 2, I met Yau Tak Yan
(姚錫祜) and Tai Zuk Ming (譚嘉明) outside Tsang Yang
Li, by arrangement, this man having previously told me that
there would be work for me to do that evening. He gave
me a number of pamphlets, which I read, and told me to
distribute them.

We all proceeded to the Tsang Hai (東海)
Primary School, Lianyung Road near Ward Road, where I threw
the pamphlets in over the wall. The other two stood
and watched whilst I did this. We then walked on a little
way, and I saw two men chalking slogans on a wall. We stood
and watched this proceeding, and a policeman came along and
arrested the two men who were chalking on the wall, my two
companions and myself.

I came to Shanghai in June last year, and studied
at the Tsang Fong (亞風) Middle School, French Concession,
until June this year, when I became a schoolteacher.

I have, and never have had, any connections with
the Communist Party.

(sgd) Tseu Chia Zung.
page_data.zh:
周家贞（女）
广州。                                          xxx        D.P.S. Nanking.
泰金路站              1936年11月3日。                              Clark Chiang

我叫周家贞，19岁，籍贯广州，居住在贝加尔路春阳里。我的职业是学校教师，在春北路梅邨浦阳小学任教。

11月2日晚上10点左右，我按约定在春阳里外遇到了姚锡祜和谭嘉明，此人此前曾告诉我那天晚上我有工作要做。他给了我一些小册子，我阅读后，他让我去分发。

我们都前往华德路附近的连云港路东海小学，我把小册子扔过了墙头。另外两人站着观看我这样做。随后我们又走了一小段路，我看到两名男子在墙上写标语。我们站着观看这一过程，这时一名警察走过来，逮捕了正在墙上写字的两名男子，以及我的两名同伴和我本人。

我去年六月来到上海，在法租界亚风中学读书，直到今年六月毕业后成为学校教师。

我过去和现在都与共产党没有任何联系。

（签名）周家贞。

page_data.en:
Tai Zuh-ming (譚若明), female
Canton                                      D.S. Makaroff
Yuling Station      3rd November            Clerk Lee Dong Liang

    My name is Tan Zuh-ming, 18 years of age, native of
Canton. My native address is Ching Chi Li Village
(清溪里), King Ping Hsien (南平縣), Canton. I
studied at the Huag Hong Middle School, King Ping Hsien,
for a period of 2 years and 8 months when my father died
and I had to leave the school. After that I became sick
for about 6 months and when I got well again, I became a
teacher at the Ching Chi Li Village, at which place I
taught students for 6 months. Soon afterwards I became
sick again and left the school staying at home for the
next 6 months. I came to Shanghai in July 1935 with a view
to entering the Wu Pang Girls School (務本), but un-
fortunately I contracted a skin disease and was unable to
enter the school. I reside in one small room at 32, Chung
Yang Lee (春陽), Daikal Road, together with another
female, named Chu Ka Tseng, a teacher of the Foo Yang
Primary School, Chenalpa Road. I am not a communist,
neither I was ever connected with any communist affairs.
All the radical literature seized in our room belongs to
my room-mate Chu Ka Tseng (周家貞). I did not know that
she is concerned or carried out the work of communists.
    This statement is true.

                                (Signed) Tai Zuh-ming
page_data.zh:
谭若明（女）
广州                                      D.S. Makaroff
榆林路站      11月3日            书记员 Lee Dong Liang

    我叫谭若明，18岁，籍贯广州。我的原籍地址是广州南平县清溪里村。我在南平县华洪中学读了两年零八个月的书，因父亲去世而不得不离校。之后我病了大约六个月，康复后，我在清溪里村当了一名教师，在那里教了六个月的学生。不久后我又生病了，离开学校在家休养了接下来的六个月。我于1935年7月来到上海，打算进入务本女中，但不幸患上了皮肤病，无法入学。我与另一名女性周家贞（Foo Yang Primary School, Chenalpa Road的教师）共同居住在大连路春阳里32号的一个小房间里。我不是共产党员，也从未参与过任何共产主义事务。在我们房间里查获的所有激进文学刊物都属于我的室友周家贞。我不知道她参与或从事共产主义工作。
    此陈述属实。

                                （签名）谭若明

page_data.en:
Yang Chi Tsau
Kiukiung xx D.S. Makareff.
Yulin Rd. Stn. 3.11.35. Clark Lee.

My name is Yang Chi Tsau (楊基朝), 19 years
of age, native of Kiukiang. My native address is Tung
Chian (東鄉) Village, Kiukiang. I began my study
at the Tei Wo (迪華) Normal School, Kiukiang, where I
studied for a period of 2 years. After the school, I
became to be an apprentice-nurse at the Kuling Medical
Mission, Kuling, where I worked for about 6 months when I
left for Shanghai. I came to Shanghai in 1933 and obtained
an employment as a clerk with the Ya Lee Waterworks Fitting
Co., Kiangse Road, near the bridge in which capacity I
worked for 18 months at the salary of $8 per month and
board and lodging. My next employment was with the Sun
Pao Circulating Library, Continental Emporium, Nanking Road,
as assistant librarian, with a salary of $10 per month. I
worked at the Sun Pao Library for a period of 6 months when it
was closed down. After that I became a private teacher
giving private lessons to a certain family, Mr.? Su Wang Li
(斯文里), Ward Road, for which work I got $8 per month
and also a small room on the premises provided by trade.
About 2 weeks ago, Tan Yaih Tsen (譚錫祚), a man arrested
together with me, came to my place, and asked me to become
a communist as a part of patriotic movement, to which I agreed
and on several occasions was given to distribute a number
of communist pamphlets on various roads in Hongkewpoo
district. I never attended any meeting neither I
participated in any other communist work.
I reside at 57 Nanking Road, Nanking Road, together
page_data.zh:
杨基朝
九江 xx D.S. Makareff.
榆林路站. 1935年11月3日. Clark Lee.

我叫杨基朝，19岁，籍贯九江。我的原籍地址是九江东乡村。我开始在九江迪华师范学校学习，在那里学习了两年。毕业后，我成为牯岭医疗传教团的一名实习护士，在那里工作了大约六个月后前往上海。我于1933年来到上海，在江西路桥附近的雅丽水管 fittings 公司（Ya Lee Waterworks Fitting Co.）找到一份职员工作，在此职位上工作了18个月，月薪8元，包食宿。我的下一份工作是在南京路大陆商场《申报》流通图书馆担任助理图书管理员，月薪10元。我在《申报》图书馆工作了六个月，直到它关闭。之后，我成为一名家庭教师，给斯文里华德路某户人家上课，这份工作月薪8元，并由雇主提供 premises 内的一个小房间。大约两周前，与我一同被捕的谭锡祚来到我住处，要求我作为爱国运动的一部分加入共产党，我同意了，并曾在虹口区各条道路上多次分发一些共产主义小册子。我从未参加过任何会议，也未参与其他任何共产主义工作。
我居住在南京路57号，与

page_data.en:
( 2 )

with Yam Tsih Tsun.    I have no communist literature
or documents in my possession.    All the books and pamphlets
seized in our room belong to Yam Tsih Tsun.
    This statement is true.

                        (Sgd)  Yung Chi Tsun.
page_data.zh:
( 2 )

严锡尊同住。我手中没有任何共产主义文献或文件。在我们房间里查获的所有书籍和小册子都属于严锡尊。
    此陈述属实。

                        （签名） 杨基尊。

page_data.en:
Tsai Chien Ping
Wusieh                               XXX   D.S. Makareff.
Yulin Rd. Sta.                  3.11.38.                     Clerk Lee

My name is Tsai Chien Ping (蔡兼平), 25 years
of age, native of Wusih. My present address is No.8 Kah
Weng Hong Lane (下王巷), Koujao (勾桥), outside of
North Gate, Wusih. I began my study at the Tsieh Yu
(积余) Primary School, where I studied for one year.
For the next year I studied English and then became a teacher
at the Sang Zah (崇实) Primary School at Wusih where I
taught students for about 6 months. My next employment
was with the Ming Tseeng (民富) Library as assistant
librarian, where I worked for 6 months when I left for
Shanghai. I came to Shanghai in 1931 and studied at the
Tung Wo Vocational School, French Concession, for a period
of 6 months. For the next 6 months I was unemployed
and then I joined the library of the Chinese Chamber of
Commerce, North Soochow Road, as assistant librarian, for a
period of one year. My salary was $15 per month. I resigned
from the above library and joined the Sun Yat Circulating
Library, Continental Emporium, Nanking Road, my salary being
$40 per month. With that library I was employed for a period
of 3 years. At the expiration of 3 years, I resigned from
the Sun Yat Circulating Library, and became assistant
librarian at the C.M. Customs Library, Tung Hoo Li (同益里)
Building Well Road, where I still work at the salary of
$35 per month. I also work on mornings only at the Information
Library, 80c. Ferguson, French Concession, for $15 per month.
On several occasions I was asked by my friend Wang Yung Nien
(王永年), unemployed, to join the Communist Party, but
page_data.zh:
蔡兼平
无锡                               XXX   D.S. Makareff.
榆林路巡捕房                  1938年11月3日                     李书记员

我叫蔡兼平，25岁，籍贯无锡。现住址为无锡北门外勾桥下王巷8号。我起初在积余小学读书，读了一年。次年我学习英语，随后在无锡崇实小学任教，教了约6个月学生。之后我在民富图书馆担任助理馆员，工作了6个月后前往上海。我于1931年来到上海，在法租界同文职业学校学习了6个月。接下来的6个月我处于失业状态，随后在北苏州路中国商会图书馆担任助理馆员，为期一年。我的月薪为15元。我从上述图书馆辞职后，加入南京路大陆商场孙逸仙流通图书馆，月薪40元。我在该图书馆工作了3年。3年期满后，我从孙逸仙流通图书馆辞职，成为同益里（Tung Hoo Li）威海卫路海关图书馆的助理馆员，目前仍在此工作，月薪35元。此外，我仅在上午在法租界福开森路80号信息图书馆工作，月薪15元。我的朋友王永年（失业）曾多次要求我加入共产党，但我

page_data.en:
(2)

I refused. All the radical literature seized in my
room was also brought to me for perusal by some Wang Too
Hyi. I don't know his address, but I know that about 2
years ago he was employed with the China Merchants Steam
Navigation Co.
I am not a communist, neither I have or have had
anything to do with Communist doctrines.

(Sgd) Tsai Chien Ping
page_data.zh:
(2)

拒绝了。在我房间内查获的所有激进文献，也是一个名叫王多义（音译）的人拿来给我阅读的。我不知道他的地址，但我知道大约两年前他在招商局轮船公司任职。
我不是共产党员，也从未与共产主义学说有任何关联。

（签名）蔡兼平

page_data.en:
To labourers throughout the country.

The month of "Red" May, (1934) comes this year in a
new era when the whole world is marching rapidly towards
revolution and war. In China, we have revolutionary warfare
and interference by anti-revolutionaries; a national crisis
caused by imperialistic invasions; the economic crisis; the
oppression by landlords and capitalists; the ever-growing
struggles of revolutionary labourers and peasants and the
lawlessness of the Fascist movement, as well as the 5th Anti-
Communist campaign of the imperialistic Kuomintang and the
heroic battles fought by the Red Armies to smash the Anti-
Communist campaign, and the rapid development of the Chinese
Soviet movement. Consequently the 5th Plenary Session
has passed the following resolution:-
"Owing to the acute revolutionary situation, the Party is
"required to strengthen a thousand-fold the revolutionary
"work of the masses. It should gain control of the masses
"by utilizing the unified battle line of the extensive
"lower grades and mobilizing the whole party in the struggles
"to overthrow the 5th Anti-Communist campaign. This is the
"most urgent and important task now confronting the party."

In directing the strikes of the proletarian classes
and in developing the revolutionary trade union movement,
the various grades of the party and labour unions should
utilize the oppression of workers by Chinese and foreign
capitalists and the treachery of the imperialistic Kuomintang
and "yellow" labour unions to achieve the object of extending
economic struggles. The greatest endeavours should be made
to prepare, organize, and direct all labour disputes, and
to form "May 1" Preparatory Committees in various factories
to organize the masses for the holding of demonstrations on
May 1. Here in Shanghai we must make immediate
page_data.zh:
致全国劳工。

今年的“红”五月（1934年）处于一个新时代，整个世界正迅速走向革命与战争。在中国，我们有革命战争和反革命势力的干涉；由帝国主义侵略引起的民族危机；经济危机；地主和资本家的压迫；革命劳工和农民斗争的不断高涨；法西斯运动的无法无天；以及帝国主义国民党发动的第五次“围剿”，红军为粉碎“围剿”而进行的英勇战斗，和中国苏维埃运动的迅速发展。因此，五中全会通过了以下决议：-
“鉴于革命形势严峻，党被‘要求千倍加强群众的革命’工作。它应通过利用广泛的下层统一战‘线来控制群众，并动员全党投入推翻第’五次‘围剿’的斗争中。这是当前党面临的最紧迫和最重要的任务。”

在指导无产阶级阶级的罢工和发展革命工会运动方面，党的各级组织和工会应利用中外资本家对工人的压迫以及帝国主义国民党和“黄色”工会的背叛，以实现扩大经济斗争的目标。应尽最大努力准备、组织和指导所有劳资纠纷，并在各工厂成立“五一”筹备委员会，组织群众举行五一示威游行。在上海，我们必须立即采取

适当措施，结合棉厂工人、码头和港口工人、造船工人及电力工人的斗争来开展抵制运动。特别是要夺取美亚绸厂工人罢工的领导权，将罢工发展为上海所有丝织工人的总罢工，并建立上海丝织工人工会。我们努力的目标是促成上海工人的总罢工，以便使我们能够掌握他们斗争的领导权。
在河北，我们应集中力量指导和发展开滦煤矿工人的总罢工，并为他们建立工会。通过指导开滦矿工的斗争，我们还能够促进和发展唐山的罢工，并组织北平的铁路工人、矿工、印刷工人，以及天津的棉厂和码头工人的斗争。
党应特别注意河北和河南沿平汉铁路的活动，因为这是帝国主义国民党从华北运送军队去攻打红军的主要线路。
在满洲，我们应加快在铁路工人、矿工、兵工厂雇员、产业工人和海员中的工作。
所有党组织都应动员其成员，以系统地开展群众运动。应说服美亚绸厂和开滦煤矿的罢工者在其他工厂的员工中公开开展活动。
不应忽视在失业工人中的活动。我们应深入失业工人集中的地区，系统地开展工作。我们应起草他们的诉求，

page_data.en:
organize an unemployment committee and a general preparatory
committee to prepare them for participation in the May 1
demonstrations. At the same time we should send out comrades
to work among the lower grade masses with a view to overthrowing
the yellow labour unions.

As regards our movement in villages, we must direct
the peasants in their opposition to usury, taxation and rentals.
In the villages in Manchuria, we should organize anti-Japanese
rural warfare and the provinces bordering on the Soviet
districts, we should organize guerilla warfare against the
Kuomintang troops/

During the month of "Red" May, 1934, we shall see a
desperate and decisive struggle between Soviet China and
Kuomintang China. Consequently, the propaganda in support
of the Red Armies should be included in our daily work. At
wharves and railways we should organize Preparatory
committees and picketing groups to oppose the transportation
of munitions and troops to fight against the Red Armies.

We should make it clear to the broad masses in
Manchuria as well as in China proper that the emancipation
of the Chinese people can be effected only by following the
example of the U.S.S.R. Consequently the protection of the
U.S.S.R. constitutes one of our main duties, and the masses
in Manchuria are required to carry out energetic activities
among railway workers, arsenal workers, seamen and Manchukuo
troops and to damage military railways, aerodromes, and other
military constructions of the Japanese imperialists who are
planning to invade the U.S.S.R. Special attention should
be paid to activities among the masses of Inner Mongolia
who should be urged to join the united battle front of Outer
Mongolia and the U.S.S.R.

Street demonstrations should be made one of the
principal tasks of the "Red" May struggles of 1934. As
page_data.zh:
组织失业委员会和总筹备委员会，为他们参加五一示威游行做准备。同时，我们应派遣同志在下层群众中开展工作，旨在推翻黄色工会。

关于我们在乡村的运动，我们必须指导农民反对高利贷、税收和地租。在满洲的乡村，我们应组织抗日农村战争；在与苏区接壤的省份，我们应组织针对国民党部队的游击战/

在1934年“红”五月期间，我们将看到苏维埃中国与国民党中国之间进行绝望而决定性的斗争。因此，支持红军的宣传应纳入我们的日常工作。在码头和铁路，我们应组织筹备委员会和纠察队，反对运输军火和部队去攻打红军。

我们应向满洲以及中国内地的广大民众阐明，中国人民的解放只有通过效仿苏联的例子才能实现。因此，保卫苏联构成我们的主要职责之一，要求满洲的群众在铁路工人、兵工厂工人、海员和伪满洲国军队中开展积极活动，并破坏日本帝国主义者计划入侵苏联的军事铁路、机场和其他军事设施。应特别注意在内蒙古群众中的活动，应敦促他们加入外蒙古和苏联的统一战线。

街头示威应成为1934年“红”五月斗争的主要任务之一。由于

Translation of Despatch "Fah" No. 1881 dated
November 19, 1935, from General Tsai Chin Chuin,
Chief of the Public Safety Bureau.
------------------------------------

To the Special Branch S.M.P.

On November 6, 1935, detectives from your
Department requested the assistance of the Special
Branch of this Bureau to arrest certain reactionary
suspects in Yung An Li Alleyway, North Szechuen Road, 永安里
etc. Four persons named Dung Fee Yau (鄧飛瑤),
Li Yu Woo (李玉荷), Dong Wei Shing (唐蕙馨) and
Loo Ser Fong (羅淑芳) were arrested and taken to the
Bureau. As the prisoner Loo Ser Fong (羅淑芳) claimed
American citizenship, he was therefore handed over to the
American Consulate through your office.

As regards the other three prisoners, each of
them has been separately interrogated. They all claim
to be law-abiding citizens and that they have never
participated in any reactionary organization. Their
statements have been found correct. They have therefore
been released after they have been ordered to furnish
security. As the prisoners were arrested upon your
request, this communication will serve to explain to you
the circumstances under which the case against the prisoners
was dealt with. I beg also to forward herewith three
photographs of the prisoners.

(Sd) Tsai Chin Chuin.

Supt. Jones
Kindly comment. I
do not recollect that we
asked whom these people
arrested.
JAS
22 NOV. 1935

J B Yao
ca.

致工部局警务处特务科

1935年11月6日，贵部侦探请求本局特务科协助，在北四川路永安里等地逮捕某些反动嫌疑人。四名名为鄧飛瑤、李玉荷、唐蕙馨和羅淑芳的人被捕并被带至本局。由于犯人羅淑芳声称拥有美国国籍，因此通过贵办事处将其移交给美国领事馆。

至于其他三名犯人，已分别进行审讯。她们均声称自己是守法公民，从未参与任何反动组织。经查证，她们的供述属实。因此，在责令她们提供担保后予以释放。由于犯人是应贵方要求被捕的，特此函告处理该案犯人的情况。另随函附上三名犯人的照片三张。

（签名）蔡劲军。

IN THE SECOND BRANCH K.I. GS. GH COURT (Asie)

Mr. King S. Kum appeared for the S.S.D. Council.
Mr. Kuh Kau Kvi appeared for the accused.

Proceedings
Mr. Kum:- During the period of remand, the police went to the American Consulate for making enquiries of the accused's nationality, but no documentary proof could be found by the American Consul-General Mr. Cunningham to prove that the accused' is really an American citizen, and here is an official letter signed by Mr. Cunningham (pro) stating that there is no definite evidence to prove actually that the accused is an American citizen. The accused was arrested on suspicion of having concerned with the other seven accused already in custody in writing communistic slogans on Liaoyang Road. At the time when those seven accused were arrested, the police found in the home of the 4th and 5th accused a note-book in which the addresses of this accused (Loo Yuk Fong) and the others named Dong, Lee, and King's were written. Therefore the police informed the P.S.B. of the matter and Dong, Lee, and King were arrested by the constables of the P.S.B., and the accused was handed over to the Settlement for making enquiries of her nationality. Now the officials of both P.S.B. and S.I.P. found that Dong, Lee, King, and this accused are in fact not concerned to communistic offence, so the former three had been released by the P.S.B. The police now found that the accused was formerly a school-mate of Daung Wei Ching when she was studying with her in the A Koo Girl School. Daung asked the accused for particulars of her address when the former left the school in order that they may exchange letters between them after they were departed. This the accused did and so her address was found written on the note-book of Daung's.

Representative of P.S.B. Dong Pan:- Our Bureau received a telephone message from the Central Station informing that 7 accused were arrested on Yulin Road for having concerned in

诉讼过程
Kum 先生：- 在还押候审期间，警方前往美国领事馆查询被告的国籍，但美国总领事 Cunningham 先生未能找到任何书面证据证明被告确为美国公民，此处有一封由 Cunningham 先生（代）签署的公函，声明没有确凿证据证明被告实际上是美国公民。被告因涉嫌与其他七名已在押被告有关联，即在辽阳路书写共产主义标语而被捕。当那七名被告被捕时，警方在第4和第5名被告家中发现一本笔记本，上面写有本案被告（Loo Yuk Fong）以及名为 Dong、Lee 和 King 的其他人的地址。因此，警方将此情况通报上海市公安局（P.S.B.），Dong、Lee 和 King 随即被上海市公安局警员逮捕，而本案被告则被移交给租界方面以查询其国籍。现在，上海市公安局和公共租界工部局警务处（S.I.P.）的官员均发现，Dong、Lee、King 及本案被告实际上并未参与共产主义犯罪，因此前三人已被上海市公安局释放。警方现查明，被告曾在爱国女校（A Koo Girl School）就读时是 Daung Wei Ching 的同学。Daung 离校时向被告索取了其详细地址，以便日后通信。被告照办了，因此她的地址出现在 Daung 的笔记本上。

Subject: Arrest of Loo Sock-fong.

Captain E. R. Kennedy,
Assistant Commissioner of Police,

Shanghai, China.

Sir,

Reference is made to your telephonic inquiries
regarding the nationality of Loo Lock-fong, a
Chinese woman arrested on November 6, 1935.

This office has searched its records without
finding any evidence to substantiate this young
woman's claim of American nationality. The young
woman and her alleged father, Loo Wai-tong, were
informed on the 6th instant that this Consulate
General would be glad to consider any evidence which
they might present in support of her claim of citi-
zenship. However, no such evidence has been pre-
sented and this office is therefore unable to inter-
cede in her behalf.

Faithfully yours,

(Sd) Edwin S. Cunningham

10 / 1 35
Date November 9, 1935

Subject Interrogation at Court of Chinese female communist suspects.

Made by D.S. Jones Forwarded by J.B. Ross O.I.

This morning D.S. Jones and D.S.I. Shih of the Special
Branch visited the House of Detention at the District Court
and interviewed the three female communist suspects named
TSEU CHIA ZUNG (周家珍), TAI ZUH MING (戴素明) and LOO SUK
FONG (羅淑芳) regarding their possible connections with other
suspects in the case. The two female suspects arrested in the
Settlement were closely interrogated with regard to the addresses
of four women found by the Police in their room at No. 32 Tsung
Yang Li (春陽里), Baikal Road. These women, LOO SUK FONG, TANG
WEI CHING (唐惠馨), LI NYI OO (李玉荷) and TSENG WEI AO (曾維奧),
were arrested at different places in Chinese territory by the
Chinese authorities because their names and addresses appeared
on slips of paper found during the search conducted at No. 32
Tsung Yang Li, Baikal Road. LOO SUK FONG, it will be remembered,
claimed United States citizenship, but her claim was not
admitted by the U.S. Consular Authorities in Shanghai. The
explanation offered by TSEU CHIA ZUNG as to how these addresses
came into her possession is that during part of 1934 they,
including herself, were schoolmates together at the AI KUO
(愛國) Middle School in Kiangwan. On leaving school, states
TSEU CHIA ZUNG, they exchanged addresses with one another, which
explains her possession of the addresses in question. According
to TSEU, she has not met any of these former schoolfellows now
under arrest since the parting last year. She states that so far
as she is aware, neither her room-mate TAI ZUH MYING (戴素明),
nor the other four detained women, have ever been engaged in
activities of a subversive nature.

During the course of our investigations into this case no
information has been obtained which could implicate in anyway
the four women arrested by the Chinese authorities.

D.S. Jones
D.C. Special Branch

主题 法庭审讯中国女性共产党嫌疑犯。

由 D.S. Jones 制作 经 J.B. Ross O.I. 转发

今天上午，特务科的 D.S. Jones 和 D.S.I. Shih 前往地方法院看守所，会见了三名女性共产党嫌疑犯，分别是 TSEU CHIA ZUNG（周家珍）、TAI ZUH MING（戴素明）和 LOO SUK FONG（羅淑芳），就她们与案件中其他嫌疑犯的可能联系进行了问询。对在租界被捕的两名女性嫌疑犯进行了严密审讯，询问关于警方在贝加尔路（Baikal Road）春阳里32号她们的房间内发现的四名女性的地址。这四名女性，即 LOO SUK FONG、TANG WEI CHING（唐惠馨）、LI NYI OO（李玉荷）和 TSENG WEI AO（曾維奧），因在贝加尔路春阳里32号的搜查中发现的纸条上出现了她们的姓名和地址，而被中国当局在华界不同地点逮捕。众所周知，LOO SUK FONG 声称拥有美国公民身份，但其主张未被上海美国领事当局承认。TSEU CHIA ZUNG 对这些地址如何落入她手中所作的解释是，在1934年的部分时间里，她们包括她自己在内，都是江湾爱国中学（AI KUO Middle School）的同学。TSEU CHIA ZUNG 称，离校时她们互相交换了地址，这就解释了她持有上述地址的原因。据 TSEU 称，自去年分别以来，她未曾见过任何这些目前被捕的前同学。她表示，据其所知，无论是她的室友 TAI ZUH MYING（戴素明），还是其他四名被拘留的女性，都从未从事过颠覆性质的活动。

在我们对该案件的调查过程中，未获得任何能将中国当局逮捕的四名女性以任何方式牵连其中的信息。

D.S. Jones
特区特务科副督察

Application is hereby made for the above described female to be detained for enquiries, she having been arrested by Officers of the S.P.S. Bureau at about 7 p.m. on 6/11/38 at No. 80 Fong Loh Li, N. Szechuen Rd, as a suspected communist.

IN THE SECOND BRANCH KIANGSU HIGH COURT (A.H.)
Mr. King & Kum appeared for the S.M. Council.

Proceedings. Mr. Kum:- The accused in this case was arrested at 7 p.m. on the 6/11/38 by Supt. Duang Pao of the Public Safety Bureau and brought to Dixwell Road Police Station at 7.05 p.m. same date for suspected communist. Supt. Duang stated that he arrested the accused at No. 80 Fong Loh Lee, off North Szechuen Road on information given by one named Duang Wei Ching who was also arrested by them for suspected communist. 指控 根据《刑事诉讼法》第76条和第101条发出的拘留令。
现申请将上述女性拘留以待查询，她因涉嫌为共产党员，于1938年11月6日晚7时许在北四川路丰乐里80号被上海市公安局（S.P.S. Bureau）警官逮捕。

江苏高等法院第二分院（A.H.）
King & Kum 先生代表上海工部局出庭。
Koh Zau Kyi 先生代表被告出庭。

诉讼过程。Kum 先生：- 本案被告于1938年11月6日晚7时被上海市公安局 Duang Pao 督察逮捕，并于同日晚上7时05分被带至狄思威路巡捕房，涉嫌为共产党员。Duang 督察称，他是在一名名为 Duang Wei Ching 的人提供情报后，在北四川路丰乐里80号逮捕了被告，Duang Wei Ching 也因涉嫌为共产党员而被他们逮捕。被告是 Duang Wei Ching（现由上海市公安局羁押）的同学。

在巡捕房，被告声称自己拥有美国公民身份。美国当局（代）向被告父亲签发了一份证书，但未附有被告的照片。经警方查询，查明被告父亲是美国公民，这通过出示其证书得到了证明。

Case No. 7/16887. Sheoi Liv. Re.

The accused claimed herself to be of American Citizenship.
Her father later attended the Police Station and produced a pass-
port bearing the photographs of three children, his wife and himself
but not the photograph of the accused.

Mr. Sawyer of the Registration Citizens Department, American
Consulate, Shanghai heard the claim, and after looking up the files
failed to find any documentary proof to show that the accused is of
American citizenship.

Questions to Accused :-

Q. Where were you born ?.
A. I was born and bred in Chung San Hsien, Canton, China.
Q. Have you been to America ?.
A. No.
Q. What is the name of your father ?.
A. My father's name is Loo Sui Leung, American citizenship.
Q. Were you arrested by the P.S.B. ?
A. Yes, they came to my home and asked me to go out saying
that one named Leung would like to see me. They searched my book
case and other articles in my house, but nothing incriminating was
found. They brought me to the Sircell Road Police Station. Leung
Wei Ching is my school mate studying in the A Koh Girls School.
Q. Do you know that Leung Wei Ching was arrested by the P.S.B.
A. I do not know.
Q. Were you an intimate friend of Leung Wei Ching ?
A. No, only a common school mate. I am not a very good friend
of her's, nor I have any grudge against her.
Q. Did you join the communist party ?.
A. No.
Q. Is your father in Court to-day ?.
A. Yes.

是一本护照。正如上述代理助理总巡官（A/M.A.）所述，那两个孩子出生在上海，我记得他们在上海美国领事馆进行了登记，但我不知道为何在那里找不到记录。

法官：- 好吧，既然你无法证明被告是美国臣民，那么她就是中国人。当你向美国领事馆申请为你女儿登记时，是否有申请表？

孙凯元（音译）先生：- 是的，有一份申请表。我不知道为什么领事馆找不到这份文件。

顾（Kuh）先生：- 法官阁下，公共安全局以涉嫌共产主义者为由逮捕了被告，但他无法提出任何证据来证实这一指控，仅仅声称一名叫张维清（Chang Wei Ching，音译）的人牵连了被告。公共安全局的官员可能讯问了他们拘留中的嫌疑人张维清是否有朋友等，该嫌疑人可能告诉他们认识被告，因此被告被捕。当然，作为公职人员，在此类涉及所谓共产主义者的案件中进行调查是他们的职责，这非常重要。但本案被告是一位非常正派的人。我看不到公共安全局逮捕她的任何理由。在缺乏针对被告的任何具体证据的情况下，我请求法官阁下准予其由可靠保释人担保释放，并可在需要时随时出庭；或者，如果公共安全局不能提出任何针对被告的证据，则应相应将其释放。

法官对顾先生说：- 如果公共安全局的代表今天不在法庭作证，则不批准被告保释。如果公共安全局不能出示针对被告的充分证据，她将自动获释。

顾先生：- 我请求法官阁下就国籍问题作出裁决，即她是中国人还是

1935年11月6日下午7时05分，上海市公安局总部督察唐豹（Dong Pas）和副督察赵宝质（Kya Wen Ping，音译）将上述一名中国女性带至本局，称他们于1935年11月6日晚7时许在四川北路旁丰乐里80号将其作为疑似共产主义者逮捕。

唐豹督察称，该女性的姓名和地址是从一名叫唐蕙荣（Dang Wei Ching，音译）的人那里获得的，此人于1935年11月6日中午12时25分在四川北路旁永安台53号被捕，也是疑似共产主义者（参见 Misc. 109/35）。

1935年11月6日晚上10时05分，南市公共安全局董宝（Dong Pao，音译）巡长和岳（Yue，音译）副巡长来到本警局，请求协助逮捕一名涉嫌为共产主义者的女性曾美清（Tsang Mei Ching，音译），25岁，学生，广东籍，居住于北四川路旁温斯洛里（Winslow Terrace）53号。警方提供协助，该女子被捕，并根据副巡捕“Y”的指示移交给公共安全局。

同上
10月6日晚上7时05分，公共安全局总部董宝（Dong Pao，音译）巡长和温平（Wen Ping，音译）未具名巡官带至本警局一名名叫陆淑芳（Loo Suk Fong，音译）的19岁中国女性，未婚，学生，广东籍，居住于北四川路丰乐里（Fong Loh Li，音译）80号，他们于10月6日晚上7时许在上述地址以涉嫌共产主义者为由将其逮捕。在警局内，该女子声称拥有美国国籍，随后她被带往美国领事馆，注册处的索耶（Sawyer）先生听取了她的申诉，并表示没有书面证据证明她是美国臣民。已通知分区巡捕“C”，被告被签发拘留令，将于今天上午出庭受审于第二特区法院。
